fields.title: Prayer – The Pulse of Life
fields.description: “Prayer – The Pulse of Life” is a book designed to offer deeper insights into the subject of prayer. While many are familiar with prayer, they often understand it in a worldly way, which is incorrect. This book draws insights from Scripture to deepen your understanding of prayer, enhance your spiritual growth, and position you for resounding success day by day, year by year. Contents: An Introduction to Prayer — Importance of Prayer — Types of Prayer — Praying With and in the Spirit — Cultivating the Spirit of Prayer — Prayer and Fasting — The First Fruit of Time — His Return — A Call to the Word — Testimonials — Prayer of Salvation.

fields.title: An Introduction To Prayer
fields.body_html:
You can only know how to pray if you first know what prayer is!

Have you ever wondered what prayer is, why people pray, or why some always pray like it’s the most important thing in their life? If so, this book is for you! Many people have learned about prayer and been blessed by what they were taught. However, some still have questions about it. I believe this book will answer most if not all, questions about prayer. So why the wait, let's go right in!

What is prayer?

1. Prayer is an honour, a privilege to fellowship and be in oneness with God. Being in oneness in this case means that one knows what is at God’s heart and is able to do w hat God tells him. With this oneness, you can know the mind of Christ, live like Christ, think like Him, and be perfect as He is. That is what prayer does, it helps you be in that fellowship, that oneness with God where you can know what to do in every situation in life. How cool that is!

2. Prayer is a two-way channel. God speaks to us and we are also privileged to talk to Him.

So, prayer is never and shouldn’t ever be considered a one -sided channel where we pray and walk away. No! God speaks too, and this is the sole purpose of prayer, to commune with God, know Him better, and get to know what His will is. In your prayer times, intentionally give God room to talk to you too. That is how you know His heart, and will.

Hallelujah!

3. Prayer is also a necessity. Luke 18:1 says: “Men ought always to pray, and not to faint” Clearly, this is not a request. The scripture doesn’t say men shall, may, can, or might pray. Rather, it says that men ought to pray and not faint. This means that prayer must be a part of your day; prayer times can also be the most interesting times in your day. So, let prayer be your lifestyle; just like how you eat even when you don’t feel like it.

Jesus Christ, the perfect example Though He knew He was the son of the Most High God, Jesus was humble enough to pray. We see this in Luke 6:12: “In these days he went out to the mountain to pray, and all night he continued in prayer to God.”

Beloved, never be too busy to pray, and never think of a time you don’t need to pray anymore.

P rayer is the pulse of every believer’s life. Without prayer, you cannot commune with God as Jesus did. Without prayer, you might not know what the Father’s will for your life is. Without prayer, it might be impossible for you to exercise your authority in Christ. This means taking up authority and causing the things that are in Christ Jesus to happen. You may also struggle to activate and walk in the consciousness of the divine presence in your life, and many more aspects that we will explain in our next chapters.

fields.title: Importance Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
Once you know how amazing something is, you can’t be forced to desire it!

There is an avalanche of benefits of prayer. As a student, knowing this is important because you will then be guided on what to expect. By learning how to pray, your spirit will be so ignited to pray more than ever. As you read what this chapter entails, let your heart and spirit be meek and open enough to feed your spirit. Take a look at these importances of prayer and let your spirit be so merry!

1. Prayer helps us commune with God. How beautiful to be one with God, united with the creator of all things, knowing what’s on His mind and knowing how exactly you can fulfil what He wants on Earth. This is so amazing!

2. Did you know that sometimes people don’t face the repercussions for their actions because someone or some people have prayed to God to have mercy upon this guilty person? That is how powerful prayer is! Your Dad, Mom, any relative or friend might have done something you don’t even think God can forgive; something big the whole world can be against, but through prayer, you can ask God to have mercy on them, and God hears when we pray. God can save your family and friends from the punishment they would have served for their actions. Glory to God! Here is a very good example in the Bible where Jesus prayed to God and lives were forgiven.

“And when they came t o the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him, and the criminals, one on his right and one on his left. And Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” Luke 23:33 -34.

So, if you have someone you would like God to forgive, go ahead and pray for them. God can have mercy on them and even get rid of the punishment they would have served had you not prayed.

3. The other importance of prayer is that it helps us to focus on God.

“Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth.” Colossians 3:2. We can set our minds on things above through prayer because prayer helps us focus, and see what God sees. Man and God are spirits so in prayer, you focus on spiritual things because you are in fellowship with God, who is a Spirit.

4. When we pray, the Holy Spirit also gives us instructions and guidance. Romans 8:26 says, “Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with g roanings too deep for words.”

Since the Holy Spirit knows the will of the Father in Heaven, He helps us communicate the will of the Father and in so, we receive guidance on how to successfully accomplish or do God’s will. Isn’t that beautiful? Without the Holy Spirit, it’s impossible to fully understand God’s will.

Acts 13:2 shows us how the disciples received instruction from the Holy Spirit as they were in fellowship with Him.

“While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

This is why every Christian should pay attention to the Holy Spirit and listen to Him.

When you pray, let the Holy Spirit guide you because He knows what God wants and what you need.

5. In prayer, we win! Hallelujah! Blessed be God! As a Christian, it’s important to know that everything that happens in the physical world first happens in the spiritual. When we pray, God makes us stronger. We have a special power from Him that helps us succeed and stay healthy. This power allows us to step on dangerous things, cast out demons in Jesus' name, and do things that seem impossible to others.

Are you facing a problem? Pray and believe that things will get better each day. God listens when we pray, and He answers. He has good plans for us, and He helps us overcome even the toughest challenges.

6. Prayer anchors us. As Christians, we don’t pray to make God change— He never changes.

We also don’t pray to get His attention because we are already impor tant to Him. We are always in His sight. Praise God! Instead, prayer helps us focus on Him. It reminds us that we are safe with Him, no matter what. That is why it’s so important to pray all the time, so we don’t give up or lose hope , but stay connected to God. Take a look at this scripture in Luke 18:1, “And he told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart.”

7. When we pray, we can speak things into existence. Your life is your responsibility, and God has given you the Holy Spirit and His Word so you can shape your world. Who you are and what you experience are a result of your words. With God’s Word, you can change situations and create new things.

When God made you, He created you in His own image, which means He wants you to be like Him — a creator. You have the power to create your own reality. For example, you can refuse to be sick because the one whose image you bear (God) can never be sick. You can choose to live a great life every day, no matter how you feel.

Some people say life has ups and downs, but I ask them, “Where does the Bible say that?” That’s not how it should be for a believer. Once I learned the truth, my life has only been going upward and forward! Praise the Lord! You have control over your life and everything in it. It’s possible to live a life of continuous success, season after season, year after year.

Speak over your life and take advantage of what God has given you. Remember, God doesn’t want you to write a new Bible; He w ants you to understand His Word and live by it. Declare prosperity and abundance with your own mouth because you are the prophet of your own life! Hallelujah!

fields.title: Types Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
“Open your mouth, and I will fill it” Psalm 81:10 Did you know how important it is to pray for yourself, your family, your neighbourhood, and even for nations and their leaders? Yes, it’s really important! Also, did you know that we pray differently depending on the season of life we are in? That’s right , because each season has its own needs.

The Bible says in Ecclesiastes that there is a time for everything, so if it's a time for joy and you are living in sorrow, you are tuning your spirit the wrong way. This is why I am going to explain the different types of prayer and when to use them. This way, you will know how to pray in each season of your life and bring about the right changes! Are you excited? Perfect, let us take a look at these types of prayer.

Prevailing Prayer Have you ever prayed, finished, and then felt like you should keep praying about something specific? It could be about your friend, your cousin, your cat or dog at home, a specific study subject, a teacher, or anything else.

Sometimes, you feel at peace that everything is taken care of after praying, but other times, you might sense that you need to keep praying, even though you have just finished praying. This can happen when the Holy Spirit is guiding you to continue praying for a certain person, situation, or issue. It doesn’t mat ter whether you're praying in tongues or in your regular language — the important thing is that you are being led to pray more. I want to talk to you about this kind of prayer: the prevailing prayer.

I remember one time when I went to a barbecue event with a friend, and for some reason, he went to the bar. I was shocked to see him, a Christian, confidently sitting in that bar like how one would sit on a cosy couch. I exclaimed, “Dear Lord Jesus!” Thoug h I tried to talk him out of that bar, nothing seemed to work. Then, I knew I wouldn’t verbally convince him out of that bar. I went to the car, locked it, and made it my prayer closet. I had an intense urge to pray, so I started speaking in other tongues as the Spirit gave me utterance. I couldn’t stop praying. The Holy Spirit is truly a wonder; within a few minutes, my friend came hurrying over, saying we had to return to the hotel immediately because we had no business at the bar! Boy, oh boy, I cried for joy. I was extremely happy because I knew it wasn’t by his own will that he left the bar so quickly, but by the Will of God. That is the power of prevailing prayer.

Prevailing prayer is powerful and continues until it brings about real change. It’s a ki nd of prayer led by the Holy Spirit, where you feel a strong urge to pray for something specific. This might take a week, a month, or even a year, but you keep praying until the result God put in your heart is achieved. Often, this kind of prayer isn't for yourself but for others — like your church, community, family, or friends. It's not about personal desires, but about praying for the good of others, just like we see in the book of Nehemiah.

In the first chapter of the book of Nehemiah, Nehemiah is told that the wall of Jerusalem is broken and its gates destroyed by fire, which deeply distresses him. Despite serving under a non- Israelite king, Nehemiah couldn't ignore the suffering of his people. He wept, confessed the sins of the people and his family, and prayed day and night before the Lord. Nehemiah had a burden on his heart, caring more about Israel than his position as King Artaxerxes' cupbearer.

Ultimately, Nehemiah successfully rebuilt the wall despite numerous challenges. Praise the Lord Jesus!

“A s soon as I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven. And I said, “O LORD God of heaven, the great and awesome God who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant that I now pray before you day and night for the people of Israel your servants, confessing the sins of the people of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Even I and my father’s house have sinned. We have acted very corruptly against you and have not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the rules that you commanded your servant Moses. Remember the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples, but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of heaven, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen, to make my name dwell there.’ They are your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand. O Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name, and give success to your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” Nehemiah 1:4 -11.

If there’s one thing to always be conscious of regarding prevailing prayer, it’s that this prayer always works if you keep praying. To succeed, you need to focus on God's Word. Refuse any negative thoughts that tell you to quit praying for your loved ones. If God told you to pray about a thing and He urged you to keep praying until you see results, keep praying, and you will be amazed by the results.

Prayer of Worship, Thanksgiving, and Praise The prayer of worship, thanksgiving, and praise is one filled with gratitude, one that exalts God and expresses his majesty, wondrous deeds, and might.

Psalms 69:30 says: ‘ I will raise the name of the Lord with songs, this shall please the Lord better than an ox that has horns and hooves .” Hebrews 13:15 “Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.” What a life!

Prayer of Intercession God wants all men to be saved and come to the knowledge of the Truth. He has done everything He needs to. “For God so loved the world that he gave his only son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life” So why don’t some people believe in Jesus Christ? Why are there people still saying that there is no God? Why do we have people rejecting the gospel of Jesus Christ?

2 Corinthians 4:3-4 (KJV) says: “But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Ch rist, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.” This means that to those who believe in Jesus Christ, the gospel is unveiled, and they can understand and live the gospel, but to those who are lost, the gospel is hidden. Why? It is because the god of this world (satan) has blinded their minds.

Do you see why it's crucial to pray for them? This kind of prayer is the intercessory prayer, one where a believer prays for others for change. In our present life, some organisations and people are working against the gospel, and God wants us to pray for them. If you don't intercede, what affects the city, nation, and world can also affect you. Recall what Mordecai told Esther: she would be affected if she didn’t intercede on behalf of the Jews. Another examp le in the Bible is that of James and Peter. James was killed, but Peter, who was also imprisoned, was spared. The difference was that believers prayed for Peter. This shows how important and mandatory prayer is, as it can save many.

Remember, intercession is about making an impact. “First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” 1 Timothy 2:1 -4.

Knowing this, if you are a Christian in a position of authority or have close connections with someone in power, like Esther, speak on behalf of the Church. You are the garrison in that place.

Use your influence and position to advance the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Prayer of Agreement “Again I say to you, if two of you agree on e arth about anything they ask, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them.” Matthew 18:19-20. There is power in agreement! When you agree on something and pray together in one accord, it can be granted to you. Note that there must be more than one person in agreement. There is specificity in all these kinds of prayers. The prayer of agreement can be done by 2 or more people.

“So Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church. Now, when Herod was about to bring him out, on that very night, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries before the door were guarding the prison. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood next to him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his hands. And the angel said to him, “Dress yourself and put on your sandals.” And he did so. And he said to him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.” And he went out and followed him. He did not know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision. When they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the Iron Gate leading into the city.

It opened for them of its own accord, and they went out and went along one street, and immediately the angel left him. When Peter came to himself, he said, “Now I am sure that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting.” Acts 12: 5 -11.

The church in Acts agreed and prayed unceasingly for Peter while he was imprisoned. The church prayed until Peter came out. You too can agree on something and it can turn around for your good.

Prayer of Faith Faith Faith Faith! What is faith? “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen” Hebrews 11:1 (KJV). What does it mean? Faith calls what is not as though it were. See how the ESV puts it. “F aith is an assurance of the things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.” Hallelujah! Knowing what faith is, what then is the prayer of faith?

Mark 11:22-23 says: “And Jesus answered them “Have faith in God. Truly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will come to pass, it will be done for him. Therefore, I tell you, whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it wi ll be yours.”

This prayer of faith involves praying to God and speaking to circumstances so that they align with your desires, without any doubt in your heart. One key aspect of this type of prayer is that it does not fail, so you should not doubt it! Stand firm on the words you speak and do not waver by saying you are unsure if it will happen.

“If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind.” James 1:5-6. Again, faith does not doubt, at all! You should maintain the right confession.

Note: For this type of prayer, you consider something done after you pray so it differs from the prevailing prayer that can be made over time until something happens. With the prayer of faith, it is done once you pray.

With all these, the Holy Spirit can guide you on what type of prayer you require to effect changes in different areas or situations in life. Yield to Him and He will guide you, always.

And I said, “O LORD God of heaven, the great and awesome God who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant that I now pray before you day and night for the people of Israel your servants, confessing the sins of the people of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Even I and my father’s house have sinned. We have acted very corruptly against you and have not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the rules that you commanded your servant Moses. Remember the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples, but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of heaven, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen, to make my name dwell there.’ They are your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand. O Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name, and give success to your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” Nehemiah 1:4 -11. If there’s one thing to always be conscious of regarding prevailing prayer, it’s that this prayer always works if you keep praying. To succeed, you need to focus on God's Word. Refuse any negative thoughts that tell you to quit praying for your loved ones. If God told you to pray about a thing and He urged you to keep praying until you see results, keep praying, and you will be amazed by the results. Prayer of Worship, Thanksgiving, and Praise The prayer of worship, thanksgiving, and praise is one filled with gratitude, one that exalts God and expresses his majesty, wondrous deeds, and might. Psalms 69:30 says: ‘ I will raise the name of the Lord with songs, this shall please the Lord better than an ox that has horns and hooves .” Hebrews 13:15 “Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.” What a life! Prayer of Intercession God wants all men to be saved and come to the knowledge of the Truth. He has done everything He needs to. “For God so loved the world that he gave his only son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life” So why don’t some people believe in Jesus Christ? Why are there people still saying that there is no God? Why do we have people rejecting the gospel of Jesus Christ? 2 Corinthians 4:3-4 (KJV) says: “But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Ch rist, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.” This means that to those who believe in Jesus Christ, the gospel is unveiled, and they can understand and live the gospel, but to those who are lost, the gospel is hidden. Why? It is because the god of this world (satan) has blinded their minds. Do you see why it's crucial to pray for them? This kind of prayer is the intercessory prayer, one where a believer prays for others for change. In our present life, some organisations and people are working against the gospel, and God wants us to pray for them. If you don't intercede, what affects the city, nation, and world can also affect you. Recall what Mordecai told Esther: she would be affected if she didn’t intercede on behalf of the Jews. Another examp le in the Bible is that of James and Peter. James was killed, but Peter, who was also imprisoned, was spared. The difference was that believers prayed for Peter. This shows how important and mandatory prayer is, as it can save many. Remember, intercession is about making an impact. “First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” 1 Timothy 2:1 -4. Knowing this, if you are a Christian in a position of authority or have close connections with someone in power, like Esther, speak on behalf of the Church. You are the garrison in that place. Use your influence and position to advance the gospel of Jesus Christ. Prayer of Agreement “Again I say to you, if two of you agree on e arth about anything they ask, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them.” Matthew 18:19-20. There is power in agreement! And behold, an angel of the Lord stood next to him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his hands. And the angel said to him, “Dress yourself and put on your sandals.” And he did so. And he said to him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.” And he went out and followed him. He did not know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision. When they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the Iron Gate leading into the city. It opened for them of its own accord, and they went out and went along one street, and immediately the angel left him. When Peter came to himself, he said, “Now I am sure that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting.” Acts 12: 5 -11. The church in Acts agreed and prayed unceasingly for Peter while he was imprisoned. The church prayed until Peter came out. You too can agree on something and it can turn around for your good. Prayer of Faith Faith Faith Faith! What is faith? “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen” Hebrews 11:1 (KJV). What does it mean? Faith calls what is not as though it were. See how the ESV puts it. “F aith is an assurance of the things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.” Hallelujah! Knowing what faith is, what then is the prayer of faith? Mark 11:22-23 says: “And Jesus answered them “Have faith in God. Truly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will come to pass, it will be done for him. Therefore, I tell you, whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it wi ll be yours.” This prayer of faith involves praying to God and speaking to circumstances so that they align with your desires, without any doubt in your heart. One key aspect of this type of prayer is that it does not fail, so you should not doubt it! Stand firm on the words you speak and do not waver by saying you are unsure if it will happen. “If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind.” James 1:5-6. Again, faith does not doubt, at all! You should maintain the right confession. Note: For this type of prayer, you consider something done after you pray so it differs from the prevailing prayer that can be made over time until something happens. With the prayer of faith, it is done once you pray. With all these, the Holy Spirit can guide you on what type of prayer you require to effect changes in different areas or situations in life. Yield to Him and He will guide you, always.

fields.title: Praying In The Spirit
fields.body_html:
We are not of this world, so we do not operate by its standards. Therefore, let us speak the language of our citizenship — the language of the Spirit.

Firstly, man is primarily a spirit with a soul, living in a physical body. When one confesses with his/her mouth that Jesus is Lord and believes in his/her heart that God raised him from the dead, that person will be saved (Romans 10:8-9). This man is then separated from the rest. 2 Corinthians 5:17 says: “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” He becomes a new creation, a superman, a man with the life of God, a man who can never be disadvantaged in life. With this, he is now in God’s kingdom, and that is where he belongs. It then becomes very vital for him/her to know the language where he/she comes from because it can help him/her stay updated on what is happening in the Kingdom.

How can one know or learn that language? You may ask.

This new creation, Superman, is given a language of the recreated spirit. That is speaking in other tongues. Some Bible versions render it differently and say it is the language of the angels. This language is not taught by men but given by God, so mere men cannot understand it because it is a divine language of God. Isn’t it beautiful speaking the language God knows so well and not even Satan can understand a word? This is praying in the Spirit. So cool!

Again, you might ask, how can I start speaking this language, speaking in other tongues? One of the answers to this is by praying to God for the infilling of the Holy Spirit, identified with speaking in tongues, and in so doing, believe that He has answered and start speaking in other tongues. As mentioned earlier, do not doubt. The other answer to this is by the laying on of hands as seen in Acts 19:6 “And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying.”

Other question might still come: “ Must every believer speak in tongues, or it is for the chosen ones? What happens if we do not pray in tongues? Don’t we have the Holy Spirit if we don’t pray in tongues? Of what benefit is prayi ng in tongues?” Let’s get right into the details, shall we?

Must all believers speak in tongues?

This question is just like asking if one must eat food. One can eat, or not, but not eating food for an extended period can negatively affect the body.

As Jesus was leaving for Heaven, He said: “ And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up serpents with their hands; and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not hurt them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.” Mark 16:17. This means that speaking in tongues is not limited to specific people; it is for all who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. No one should condemn it or say that it is only for certain individuals. Since you are a spirit and God is a spirit too, speaking the spirit language should be a priority.

Speaking in tongues is a sign that one has been filled with the Spirit The disciples were waiting for the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. They were in one accord.

Cloven tongues as of fire sat upon each of them. Look at Acts 2:4. “And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

In the Old Testament, the Holy Spirit came upon kings, priests, and judges so that they could carry out the work and teach God’s people. So He first sat upon them as tongues of fire. After, He filled them. However, in the New Testament, the Holy Spirit dwells in us and makes us His temple. He comes upon you to fill you. The evidence that you are filled with the Holy Spirit is the evidence of the sign of speaking in tongues. Being with the Holy Spirit and being filled with the Holy Spirit are not the same things. Those that are filled with the Holy Spirit speak in other tongues. So, speaking in tongues is not meant for the pastors, Bishops, and evangelists alone, it is for everyone.

Why then should you speak in tongues?

1. It builds you up “The one who speaks in a tongue builds up hims elf, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.” 1 Corinthians 14:4. To edify means to build, to construct, and to establish. Jude 1:20 (AMP) says: “But you, beloved, build yourselves up on [the foundation of] your most holy faith [continually progress, rise like an edifice higher and higher], pray in the Holy Spirit. ” So he tells us to build ourselves in the most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit. That is how important praying in tongues is. As you speak in tongues, you are edified, and you become bigger than the circumstances you are facing. Beautiful, isn’t it?

Are you facing a challenge or a condition that seems to have no solution? Is it about your health, your family, your community, or the nation? You have the power to effect changes in everything that concerns you. Speak in tongues, keep speaking in tongues, and changes will be effected.

Hallelujah!

2. Speaking in tongues charges you up In the same book of 1 Corinthians, the one who speaks in tongues edifies themselves. This word also means charging up. When you speak in other tongues, you are generating power and energy.

Did you charge up in the morning? As you go to class, charge up. Before going to church, charge up. When you start studying, you will operate well because you have charged up. Praise the Lord!

4. Speaking in other tongues refreshes you As a Christian, whenever you feel the need to cool down, perhaps when your mind is overwhelmed with anything, any issue, speaking in tongues refreshes you. God can speak to you, guide you, and bring you peace during those moments. “For by people of strange lips and with a foreign tongue the LORD will speak to this people” Isaiah 28 11.

5. Speaking in tongues allows us to fellowship with the Holy Spirit When we speak in tongues, we are speaking the language of the Holy Spirit. It's a way to relate with Him and receive His wisdom, courage, and boldness. This is why everyone should speak in tongues. When you speak in tongues regularly, you can never be defeated. You will know what to do and you will be guided by the God of Heaven and Earth, ensuring you stay on the right path. Hallelujah!

fields.title: Cultivating The Spirit Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
Whatever you intentionally cultivate grows!

Who is the Spirit of Prayer?

“ Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.” Romans 8:26 The spirit of prayer is the Holy Spirit, and He is the one who intercedes on our behalf. Through us, He maintains an atmosphere of prayer in our lives. Everyone should have Him! Whether we notice it or not, He operates powerfully in us, and without Him, nothing can be done perfectly.

We receive and invite Him by desire. We receive Him the same way we received the Lord Jesus Christ in our lives; by faith. You cannot perform an act to get the Holy Spirit, not even the good deeds can make Him come or even fill you. It is by desire and faith.

The Holy Spirit is truly wonderful. If you are thirsty, He will satisfy you. You will find yourself praying continually. He will lead you into His visions, plans, and purposes. He will express Himself through you in prayer, and you will know that He is at work! Everyone needs to have the Spirit of prayer because He is the perfect guide in all things.

One might say: “I have prayed and invited the spirit of prayer to influence my life but I am not seeing any change.” I will respond to this with an example of a m other who wants her children to accept the Lord Jesus and be born again. She is praying for her children to see Jesus so that they can go to church as a whole family. Have you noticed where the problem is coming from? The problem is in the reason/motive for praying. It is a marvelous thing to pray for souls to come to Christ, but if the motive is for personal pleasure, it ceases to be a powerful prayer because it is selfish. “You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it on your passions.”

James 4:3. Our focus should be on eternity. Perhaps this is why someone hasn't seen any change even after praying for the Spirit of prayer. As you pray for your friend, teacher, sister or any other person, always remember to have the right reason for what you are praying for.

How then can we cultivate the Spirit of Prayer? How can we fully benefit from the Holy Spirit? How can we nurture the Spirit of Prayer?

1. By praying at all times in the Spirit, having faith, and letting it be proven that you operate by faith and not by sight. This means that you can call things that are not as though they are. You can command the situation to change because the power is in you. You are stronger than 10,000 armies! Stronger than malaria, ulcers, cancer, hepatitis, fibroids, HIV, sickle cells, tumours, and any other sickness or disease. Praise the Lord! Pray in the Spirit, release mysteries because you have the power to effect changes in your life.

2. We cultivate the Spirit of prayer through meditating on God’s Word. T hrough it, the Holy Spirit can be stirred and can cause us to pray fervently. The more you read the Word, the more you know it, and if you can put to work what you have known, and meditate on it always, you can never be discouraged or disadvantaged. You always grow because you are feeding and acting on the word of God, and that stirs up the Spirit of Prayer. Diseases can’t thrive in such atmospheres, sicknesses can’t, and neither can sorrow, condemnation, or worry!

fields.title: Prevailing In Prayer
fields.body_html:
We first prevail with God before we prevail with men.

In the context of prayer, prevailing prayer means one that continues with persistence until it achieves the desired outcome. Before we move any further, I would like us to remember that we win in the spirit first before the victory is seen in the physical. See how Jacob wanted to return to his homeland. All of what God had blessed him with was taken and he was ready to go home.

However, he remembered that he had cheated his brother Esau. Esau was now established, giving Jacob ample reason to be afraid. As he prepared for the journey, his heart was unsettled, and he found himself alone. Jacob understood that unless he prevailed with God, he wouldn't prevail with Esau.

That night, an angel appeared to Jacob, and he wrestled with the angel until morning. Jacob didn’t give up; he held on until the angel blessed him. This showed that Jacob had won with God, preparing him to succeed with Esau.

“Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed.” Genesis 32:28.

Unlike our usual prayers, prevailing prayer arises from a deep burden on one's heart. It's the kind of prayer the Holy Spirit compels you to continue until you see results. As discussed earlier, prevailing prayer is essential; it doesn't stop until it achieves its purpose. It goes beyond simply thanking the Lord for His goodness; it involves intense prayer.

“Likewise , the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.” Romans 8:26.

Without the Holy Spirit, one cannot prevail in prayer because nothing, or so little can be changed when we pray carnally. Why? We cannot know what exactly is right to say, and how to say it to effect changes but the Spirit is our guide.

Do you feel like you have done everything but still not seeing results? Keep going! Don't stop until you succeed. Even if it doesn't seem to work, it actually is. The enemy knows you can win if you keep pressing on. He only bothers with people who give up because he knows they've already lost. So, don’t give up! If you feel a burden to pray, make sure you do. God won’t give you more than you can handle. Whatever He gives you, He also gives you the strength to overcome! Hallelujah!

But before praying, repenting of anything wrong in your life is important. After that, receive forgiveness and move on. Speak in other tongues as it helps you accomplish things that are needed for that matter. Then, speak the word of God with boldness. When the Holy Spirit fills your heart, you speak the word of God with boldness “And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.” Acts 4:31.

What does prevailing prayer do?

It maintains inspiration. If you are not praying, you will lose the favour/glow that follows it. “Do not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, and serve the Lord.” Romans 12:11. Never lag in zeal!

How do you do it? By meditating on the word of God. Do that again and again, and let it become a part of you.

Prevailing prayer also cleanses and makes us more glorious than we came in before prayer. The more you pray, the more you glow.

Whatever He gives you, He also gives you the strength to overcome! Hallelujah! But before praying, repenting of anything wrong in your life is important. After that, receive forgiveness and move on. Speak in other tongues as it helps you accomplish things that are needed for that matter. Then, speak the word of God with boldness. When the Holy Spirit fills your heart, you speak the word of God with boldness “And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.” Acts 4:31. If you are not praying, you will lose the favour/glow that follows it. “Do not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, and serve the Lord.” Romans 12:11. Never lag in zeal! How do you do it? By meditating on the word of God. Do that again and again, and let it become a part of you. Prevailing prayer also cleanses and makes us more glorious than we came in before prayer. The more you pray, the more you glow.

fields.title: Prayer And Fasting
fields.body_html:
The fast is on because you’re praying, not because you’re not eating.

When we talk about prayer and fasting, some people think it just means not eating, like eating would be a mistake! It sounds funny, but it’s a common misunderstanding. Many people focus only on the idea of fasting as a time to avoid food, missing the true purpose.

Fasting isn't just about skipping meals —it’s about replacing food with time spent in prayer and focusing on God's Word. If you’re just not eating and sleeping all day to pass the time, that’s not fasting —that’s just starving yourself.

As Christians, we need to understand that fasting is about prayer. We fast because we’re praying, not just because we aren’t eating. It's a call to spend time in prayer, and as we do that, we make a conscious decision to refrain from eating.

Acts 13:2 says, “As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Spirit said...” Notice the order: they ministered to the Lord and fasted. How do you minister to the Lord? Through praise, thanksgiving, worship, and prayer. The focus was on ministering to the Lord, and because of this, they fasted.

The Bible additionally shows us that after the Lord spoke to them after they had prayed. This is one of the benefits of prayer and fasting; you can receive guidance from the Holy Spirit, which can save you from countless mistakes.

Besides receiving guidance, prayer, and fasting, attune your spirit to the things of God more deeply.

Through prayer and fasting, you are ministering to the Lord. So, spend time in prayer and fasting.

Some people say they are fasting but spend the day sleeping or engaging in irrelevant activities to distract themselves from hunger. I used to be like that, but praise the Lord, the Holy Spirit guided me on how to pray and fast effectively. Prayer and fasting should focus on prayer and activities that encourage prayer, such as studying the Bible, worshipping the Lord, praising, and meditating on the Word. Hallelujah!

Turn off your phone if it will distract you. While many people enjoy receiving updates, it is more important to receive updates from the Spirit realm during this time. Turn off your TV and set aside any newspapers or magazines. Focus on activities that encourage you to pray. As mentioned earlier, it is much better to begin by speaking in tongues, which is praying in the Spirit. This way, you will be guided on what to say in your understanding; the Holy Spirit will lead you in what to pray.

One might ask, “When should I fast? Should I fast every day, month, or once a year?”

Firstly, it is an excellent time to fast when your local church, school fellowship or congregation declares a prayer and fasting program. Never separate yourself from such a call, thinking you don't feel the need to pray and fast yet, or that you will do it at your own perfect time. No, it shouldn't be that way. There are things we do together as a community, such as corporate worship, and many other activities intended for spiritual growth and edification; prayer and fasting are among them.

If your church calls for prayer and fasting, do not refuse to participate and instead set your times for starting or ending the fast. This approach is wrong. Exercise discipline and fast as instructed.

This is how you bring about changes in the spiritual realm. Remember, through this practice, your ability to hear and receive from God is sharpened, and you become more attuned to spiritual matters. The more you pray and fast, the less likely you are to be caught off guard because you can perceive things that are about to happen and influence what you want to see in your life and the lives of those around you. Hallelujah!

Secondly, fast when the Holy Spirit leads you to do so, or when you choose to fast and pray. This is another perfect opportunity, especially if it's the Spirit guiding you; you will recognise His leading. Take it seriously and proceed with the fast.

Some people schedule prayer and fasting days or moments as a spiritual discipline, and that's beautiful. Therefore, whenever and however you are guided to fast, take it seriously. Make prayer and fasting a part of your spiritual routine.

fields.title: The First Fruit Of Time
fields.body_html:
How you start your day tells a lot about how the rest of the day will be!

Would you like your day to feel like Heaven on Earth? Think about your daily routine — how do you start your mornings? What are your priorities, and what’s the first thing you do? If prayer isn’t at the top of your list, it might be time to switch things up.

Here’s something powerful: everything that happens in the physical world has already been set in motion in the spiritual world. As Christians, we can create because we’re made in God’s image.

That’s why it’s so important to take control and intentionally shape your day. Many people wake up and set their intentions, and if you’re not careful, you might end up living according to someone else’s plans or prayers.

What you do in the first hour of your day matters. Make it a habit to wake up early and bless your day with prayer. When you do this, you’ll notice your day becomes clearer, and everythi ng feels smoother. Plus, you open yourself up to receiving guidance from God, who wants you to succeed and prosper. Let Him direct your path, and you’ll be amazed at how your life is transformed!

fields.title: His Return!
fields.body_html:
Prepare yourself to meet the Lord Jesus Christ!

“And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in perplexity because of the roaring of the sea and the waves, people fainting with fear and with foreboding of what is coming on the world. For the powers of the heavens will be shaken. And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. Now when these things begin to take place, straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.” Luke 21:25 -28 Many signs are showing us where we are today and how close we are to the time when nations will be judged. No matter where you are right now, always remember that Jesus Christ is coming soon.

Some believe and are eagerly waiting for His return, while others are sceptical and not expecting Him. But He is coming, so prepare yourself for Him. He is coming for “...all who have loved his appearing.” (2 Timothy 4:8), those who are ready for Him. The Bible says blessed are those who are waiting for His return (Luke 12:37).

While at school, home, or anywhere else, live your life as though His return could happen at any moment because it can indeed happen at any moment. 1 Corinthians 15:52 tells us, “ In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we shall be changed. ” It has been almost two thousand years since Jesus Christ ascended from this world. The prophecies ab out His coming are being fulfilled before our eyes. He said: “Surely I come quickly…” (Revelation 22:20).

Statistics show that today's world is crueler, violent, and filled with terrorism than ever before.

Life's challenges are tougher now than they’ve ever been. So, don’t get caught off guard. Stay in Christ, live in righteousness, and keep living for Him. Illuminate your world with the Gospel by preaching the gospel and winning souls to the Lord Jesus Christ. Your reward is great.

As the world is changing, refuse to succumb to its pressure because greater is He that is in you than he that is in this world. Christ has given you power over all things. Be unshakeable. Live above the systems of the world.

Christ is coming back! It is not a story or a myth, it is about to happen!

Dedicate your time, resources, and energy to spreading the Gospel until it reaches the ends of the earth. Prepare yourself and help others prepare for the rapture of the church, too.

fields.title: A Call To The Word
fields.body_html:
If you want to know the will of God, know His word!

In many meetings, I encourage Christians to make it a priority to know what God wants us to do.

The truth is, you can't know God's plan for your life if you don't read the Bible. It's like a manual for living, meant to shape who we are.

If you want to understand your purpose and what God has planned for you, spend time in prayer and read His Word. A Christian who doesn’t read the Bible is missing out on the de eper things of God. Loving God means wanting to know what pleases Him — and we learn that through His Word.

If life feels tough or the world seems overwhelming, the Bible is where you’ll find strength, hope, and guidance. God's Word gives life! It restores, saves, and even heals. When the Bible says you are the head and not the tail, believe it, and live it!

There’s so much peace and power that come from living God’s Word. Sorrow, fear, and worldly troubles won't shake you because you know that's not your portion. The Bible gives you the direction you need every day. Read it, believe it, and boldly live out what it says about you.

You are not like everyone else. You’re chosen, special, and called to show God’s goodness in the world. You are the light of the world, set apart to radiate His glory. With God living in you, you’re unstoppable and unshakable. Hallelujah!

fields.title: Testimonials
fields.body_html:
He has done great things, and we bless His name!

It's exciting to share stories of prayers that were answered! In this chapter, you’ll see examples of people who prayed and experienced amazing results. Some stories come from the Bible, and others are real-life testimonies from today’s church. God never stops answering prayers, especially when we pray in Jesus' Name. Check out these inspiring examples of people who prayed and saw victory!

Received Strength Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, prayed. Though purely divine, he was also purely human. Through prayer, Jesus was strengthened. “And there appeared to h im an angel from heaven, strengthening him.” Luke 22:43.

Received a Son Hannah is also one of the women who prayed and prevailed. She was one of the two wives of Elkanah, a Levite who lived at Ramah. Despite the fact that she was married, she had no children, and that upset her. She cried unto the Lord, and she prevailed. She gave birth to a son whom she called Samuel. Samuel was given unto the Lord, and he did mighty exploits as we see in 1 st and 2 nd Samuel.

Shamed All Prophets of Baal Another was Elijah, who prayed for fire to come down from Heaven (1 Kings 18). When the people of Israel turned away from God and worshipped false gods, especially the false god of Baal, Elijah prayed for fire on Mount Carmel. This was to prove the only true God. With the prophets of Baal praying to their God for a response, Elijah prayed after their god did not answer. The Lord God of Hosts answered by sending fire from Heaven. He prevailed!

Others from the Bible include David, Jonah, Esther, and Job.

Rescued from a terrible accident Among those outside the Bible is myself. I got into a terrible accident during my O-Level holidays. I was hit by a motorcycle and almost taken over by a car on the same road, but thanks be to God, I was saved. No one knew that I would make it; some thought that I was not mentally okay when I stood up, but God is great. When I called upon the Lord, He saved me! Here I am 10 years later, so beautiful and healthy! Glory to God!

Healed from HIV/AIDS At my local church, there is a lady who was diagnosed with HIV/AIDS. She was sick all the time, and many, including some believers, lost hope, but she didn’t! She kept on praying and believing God for greater things even though she looked like she was about to die. Finally, she was healed by the power of God. It has been more than 15 years since she was healed, and she is still negative to this day! Praise the Lord!

Got her results Biyinzika sat for her university exams but was never given marks. As many told her to repeat those papers, she refused and prayed. God answered her prayers, and the marks that were allocated on her academic papers were so excellent that they were a marvel.

Got a job Exceeding her expectations, Precious got a well-paying job at one of the biggest companies in the country after praying. She had finished school but hadn’t found a placement. Through prevailing prayer, she was able to see results, that were beyond her comprehension. Glory to God!

Isn’t the Lord amazing? Absolutely! And guess what —those aren’t the only testimonies! No matter what you’re facing, there’s nothing God can’t handle. Nothing is too big for Him!

Surrender it all to God, pray, and watch the testimonies roll in! Hallelujah!

fields.title: Prayer Of Salvation
fields.body_html:
Christianity is not a religion; it is living the God-kind of life.

God loved the world so much that He gave His Son, Jesus Christ, to die for everyone. Why? So that you and I would not perish but have everlasting life! Oh wow! I have everlasting life, and so do you if you are born again. If you are not yet born again, this moment is your opportunity. You will have eternal life if you believe in Jesus Christ with your heart and declare Him Lord over your life!

“But you said Jesus Christ died for everyone, why then say it is only those who are born again that have eternal life?” You may ask. I will start by giving an example of a friend saying that they have signed a cheque for you. As it is known, money is yours. However, if you don’t mo ve to the bank to pick up your money and instead throw your cheque away, you won’t have that money, even when they signed it for you. This is the same thing with eternal life. Our Lord, Jesus Christ, died for the entire world. However, eternal life is imparted to those who believe in our Lord Jesus as the Son of the living God, believing that He came, died, and was raised again and is alive today. When you know, accept, and confess that Jesus Christ is the Lord of your life, eternal life is immediately imparted in your spirit. That is how eternal life is received. Praise the Lord!

Would you now want to receive this eternal life, the God-Kind of life? I hereby invite you to make Jesus Christ the Lord of your life, if you haven’t. Kindly believe and pray thus : “O Lord God, I believe with all my heart in Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God. I believe He died for me and God raised Him from the dead. I believe He is alive today. I confess with my mouth that Jesus Christ is the Lord of my life from this day. Through Him and in His Name, I have eternal life; I am born again. Thank you, Lord, for saving my soul! I am now a child of God. Hallelujah!”

Congratulations! You are now a child of God, born of the Word of God. You are a new creature that is so perfect and righteous because Christ the Lord now lives in you, and has made you His righteousness. You don’t need to feel it but believe that you are n ow a different person, so victorious and can now make the wisest decisions ever. Nothing is impossible for you now! Start reading the Bible and allow God to speak and guide you in His perfect will.

God bless you!

THE END
